newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks still set for traditional year end rally.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks still set for traditional year end rally.

text.p: UK traders said London's stock market still looks on course for its traditional year-end rally, breaking from its post-budget lethargy and shaking off nagging worries over inflationary pressures and rising interest rates.

"December is normally a bullish month for the market. If you go back to 1969 the all-share has risen in 70 percent of Decembers and 78 percent of all Januarys," said Nick Glydon, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities.
But some analysts say the FTSE 100 could initially test support at 4,000 before building up momentum to retest highs.
"The critical levels are 4,100 and 4,000," Glydon said. "4,000 is an important support level but if we break 4,100 I think we will see a quick advance in December."
"The market is trying to rally at the moment and we could break 4,100 next week," Glydon added "Today's breakout by gilts is also a very bullish sign."
The FTSE 100 index was up 7.4 points at 4,057.4 by 1512 GMT on Friday. The December long gilt future contract was up 25/32 at 111-24/32.

Other European bourses were making sharp gains, driven by a stronger dollar but in London the pound soared to a 33-month peak against the mark as a rise in British interest rates looked increasingly likely.

A string of economic data and major company results next week could help to improve sentiment and kickstart the FTSE's advance but U.S. payrolls data due on Friday are likely to take centre stage as Wall Street's performance continues to set the trend.

Domestic companies scheduled to report earnings on Monday include Scottish and Newcastle with half year results. On Tuesday Siebe Plc will post interims and Wednesday sees third quarter figures from Kingfisher and full year profits from Bass and Carlton Communications.
Thursday's results include Great Universal Stores, Grand Metropolitan and Hanson with General Electric's half year results ending the week on Friday.
Investors will also have plenty of domestic economic data to chew over with money supply numbers on Monday along with the latest purchasing managers index.
Tuesday will include data on official reserves and the CBI's distributive trades survey will be released on Thursday with new housing starts and completions.
On Friday, construction, manufacturing, and output data are scheduled but U.S. Payrolls figures will doubtless be the focus of attention.
